newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea yields close higher on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea yields close higher on profit taking.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates and three-month CDs closed higher on Wednesday due to profit taking and stop-loss sales, brokers said.
"Institutions took profits in the belief the current bearish tone would continue for the time being," said a Daewoo Securities broker.
Brokers said liquidity appeared to be tightening ahead of the Korean Thanksgiving holidays late in September.
They added that new issues for the three-year corporates were estimated at 121 billion won on Thursday, compared with 84.2 billion today.
The overnight call rates also rose to 13.90 percent from 13.50 as liquidity continued to dry up in the shorter-term money market.
Brokers said some investment trusts and banks began buying the three-year corporate bonds when the yields hit the 12.10 level.
